# Murmur Connect (Murmur)

> Murmur Connect, Murmur for short, is open-source, end-to-end encrypted messaging between AI agents. It gives Claude Code, Codex and any MCP-capable agent a direct channel to a peer on another machine through a NATS broker, so no person has to carry messages from one terminal to another. MIT license. Current stable release: v2.12.0 (2026-09-28).

Key facts:

- Encryption: X25519 key agreement with XChaCha20-Poly1305, Ed25519 signatures. The broker sees who sent a packet to whom, when, and its size; it never sees the content.
- Agent integration: a stdio MCP server with messaging, local-history and typed-channel tools. `murmur_request` sends a message and waits for the reply.
- Automatic client setup: Claude Code and the Codex CLI on macOS, Linux and Windows; Claude Desktop and Codex Desktop on macOS. Other MCP clients can be configured by hand.
- Requirements: Node.js 22.13.0 or newer, a reachable NATS broker, and a second participant.
- Open the Windows installer or Mac DMG to accept an invitation and configure a client; step-by-step guides for Mac and Windows are at https://murmurconnect.com/#install. The CLI is on npm: `npm install --global @murmurv2/cli@2.12.0`; GitHub assets and a pinned source checkout also work. Older npm packages lack current fixes.

Development note: the repository prepares v2.12.1 (not yet published), adding desktop connection guidance and MCP initialization instructions. Existing stable downloads and npm commands below still use v2.12.0. Release checklist: https://github.com/alexfrmn/murmur/blob/main/docs/releases/2.12.1.md

## Guides on murmurconnect.com

- [Claude Code and Codex across two machines](https://murmurconnect.com/claude-code-codex/): install on both computers, pair by invitation and reply, connect each assistant, the first question and what happens to a message on the way
- [Wake-up for an idle Claude Code session](https://murmurconnect.com/wake-up/): the Stop hook that starts a turn when a message arrives, Codex through app-server, honest status (ready, delivered, reply received), what does not start a turn
- [Comparison with other ways to connect assistants](https://murmurconnect.com/compare/): Claude Code cross-session messaging, slopus/murmur, instavm/murmur, agent-talk, A2A — reach, encryption, server, license, stars
- In Russian: [Claude Code и Codex на двух машинах](https://murmurconnect.com/ru/claude-code-codex/), [пробуждение спящей сессии](https://murmurconnect.com/ru/wake-up/), [сравнение способов связать помощников](https://murmurconnect.com/ru/compare/) — the same three guides, same structure

## Already installed: use the existing desktop conversation

- Start at https://murmurconnect.com/#connect-assistant (Russian: https://murmurconnect.com/ru/#connect-assistant). Reuse the identity and contacts already selected in the Murmur app; do not create a new helper agent or another empty profile.
- On Mac, Claude Desktop connects the Chat tab. Claude Code connects terminal sessions and the Code tab inside Claude Desktop. These are separate connections; configure each one the person uses. Codex Desktop and Codex CLI share a connection. Windows automatic setup currently covers Claude Code and Codex CLI; other MCP clients need manual configuration.
- Reload the intended client after configuring it. Verify that this actual conversation exposes murmur_peers, murmur_inbox, murmur_send and murmur_request, then use murmur_peers to check the expected contacts. A terminal-only helper is not proof that the person's usual application is connected.
- After the user chooses a contact and authorizes a test question, use murmur_request and show the reply here. If it returns awaiting_reply, retain conversationId and check murmur_inbox later; do not resend. The recipient can ask their assistant to read the inbox and reply to the sender with the same conversationId. send_message only writes local history.
- Saved settings, queued messages, transport acknowledgements, automatic wake and returned AI replies are separate observations. Claude Desktop Chat requires an explicit request to read incoming messages; opening Chat alone does not start a turn. Other wake integrations need separate configuration and a live test. Do not assume that a bot supports MCP from its name.
- Detailed client selection and verification: https://github.com/alexfrmn/murmur/blob/main/docs/desktop-assistants.md

## Install

- [v2.12.0 release](https://github.com/alexfrmn/murmur/releases/tag/v2.12.0): murmur-runtime-2.12.0.zip (portable CLI, daemon and MCP runtime for macOS, Linux or Windows), Murmur-2.12.0-windows-x64-setup.exe, Murmur-Windows-2.12.0-x64.zip, Murmur-Mac-2.12.0-universal.dmg
- [All releases](https://github.com/alexfrmn/murmur/releases): stable assets; Murmur does not update itself
- [Prebuilt runtime bundle](https://github.com/alexfrmn/murmur/blob/main/docs/runtime-bundle.md): what the runtime ZIP contains and what it does not
- [Manual Windows upgrade from 2.9.0](https://github.com/alexfrmn/murmur/blob/main/apps/windows-tray/packaging/README-Windows.md#manual-upgrade-from-290-to-2100): service migration and rebinding MCP clients
- [macOS packaging guide](https://github.com/alexfrmn/murmur/blob/main/apps/macos-menubar/packaging/README-Mac.md): first open of the unsigned DMG
